title: Best Streak of Daily Scores
statement: A student logs a score change every day (positive or negative). Find the largest total change over any run of consecutive days (at least one day).
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.
reference_solution:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
best = cur = a[0]
for x in a[1:]:
    cur = max(x, cur + x)
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)
hints: What is the best sum of a run that must END at day i?
This is Kadane's algorithm (a 1-D DP).
Keep cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]) and track the maximum cur seen.

statement: For each team member i, print the product of everyone else's contribution scores. Division is not allowed.

import sys

title: Run-Length Encoder
statement: Compress a lowercase string by replacing each run of identical characters with the character followed by the run length. Example: aaabbc becomes a3b2c1.
input_format: One line: s.

import sys

out = []
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    out.append(s[i] + str(j - i))
    i = j
print("".join(out))

title: Friend Circles
statement: n students and m undirected friendships are given. Print the number of friend circles (connected components).
input_format: Line 1: n m. Next m lines: u v (1-indexed).
reference_solution:
import sys
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, m = d[0], d[1]
parent = list(range(n + 1))
def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; x = parent[x]
    return x
comps = n
for i in range(m):
    a, b = find(d[2 + 2 * i]), find(d[3 + 2 * i])
    if a != b:
        parent[a] = b; comps -= 1
print(comps)
hints: Each friendship can merge two groups.
Use BFS/DFS or Union-Find (disjoint set union).
Start with n components and decrement each time a union joins two different roots.

title: Fewest Bus Hops
statement: Bus stops 1..n are connected by m undirected routes. Print the minimum number of routes needed to go from stop 1 to stop n, or -1 if it is impossible.
input_format: Line 1: n m. Next m lines: u v (1-indexed).
reference_solution:
import sys
from collections import deque
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, m = d[0], d[1]
g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for i in range(m):
    u, v = d[2 + 2 * i], d[3 + 2 * i]
    g[u].append(v); g[v].append(u)
dist = [-1] * (n + 1); dist[1] = 0
q = deque([1])
while q:
    u = q.popleft()
    for v in g[u]:
        if dist[v] == -1:
            dist[v] = dist[u] + 1; q.append(v)
print(dist[n])
hints: All routes have the same cost.
Breadth-first search finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
BFS from stop 1, storing the distance when each stop is first discovered.

title: Course Prerequisites
statement: There are n courses. Each of m lines 'a b' means course b must be completed before course a. Print YES if it is possible to finish all courses, otherwise NO.
input_format: Line 1: n m. Next m lines: a b.
reference_solution:
import sys
from collections import deque
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, m = d[0], d[1]
g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]; indeg = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(m):
    a, b = d[2 + 2 * i], d[3 + 2 * i]
    g[b].append(a); indeg[a] += 1
q = deque(i for i in range(1, n + 1) if indeg[i] == 0)
done = 0
while q:
    u = q.popleft(); done += 1
    for v in g[u]:
        indeg[v] -= 1
        if indeg[v] == 0:
            q.append(v)
print("YES" if done == n else "NO")
hints: When is it impossible to finish everything?
Detect a cycle in a directed graph (topological sort).
Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take courses with in-degree 0; all n must be taken.

title: Cheapest Delivery Route
statement: A delivery network has n hubs and m one-way roads with non-negative costs. Print the minimum cost from hub 1 to hub n, or -1 if hub n is unreachable.
input_format: Line 1: n m. Next m lines: u v w.
reference_solution:
import sys, heapq
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, m = d[0], d[1]
g = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for i in range(m):
    u, v, w = d[2 + 3 * i], d[3 + 3 * i], d[4 + 3 * i]
    g[u].append((v, w))
INF = float("inf"); dist = [INF] * (n + 1); dist[1] = 0
pq = [(0, 1)]
while pq:
    du, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
    if du > dist[u]:
        continue
    for v, w in g[u]:
        if du + w < dist[v]:
            dist[v] = du + w; heapq.heappush(pq, (dist[v], v))
print(dist[n] if dist[n] < INF else -1)
hints: BFS is not enough because roads have different costs.
Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap.
Pop the closest hub, relax its outgoing roads, and skip stale heap entries.

title: Longest Rising Streak
statement: Print the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of the array (not necessarily contiguous).
input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.
reference_solution:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_left
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = d[0]; tails = []
for x in d[1:1 + n]:
    i = bisect_left(tails, x)
    if i == len(tails):
        tails.append(x)
    else:
        tails[i] = x
print(len(tails))
hints: An O(n^2) DP works; can you do better?
Patience sorting: keep the smallest tail for each length.
For each x, binary-search the first tail >= x and replace it (or append).

title: Shared Skill Sequence
statement: Two strings describe skill sequences. Print the length of their longest common subsequence.
input_format: Line 1: a. Line 2: b.
reference_solution:
import sys
a, b = sys.stdin.read().split()[:2]
prev = [0] * (len(b) + 1)
for ca in a:
    cur = [0] * (len(b) + 1)
    for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
        cur[j] = prev[j - 1] + 1 if ca == cb else max(prev[j], cur[j - 1])
    prev = cur
print(prev[-1])

title: Hackathon Backpack
statement: You can carry at most W kg of gadgets to a hackathon. Each gadget has a weight and a usefulness value and can be taken at most once. Print the maximum total value.
input_format: Line 1: n W. Next n lines: weight value.
reference_solution:
import sys
d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, W = d[0], d[1]
dp = [0] * (W + 1)
for i in range(n):
    w, v = d[2 + 2 * i], d[3 + 2 * i]
    for cap in range(W, w - 1, -1):
        dp[cap] = max(dp[cap], dp[cap - w] + v)
print(dp[W])
hints: Greedy by value/weight ratio does not always work for 0/1 items.
Classic 0/1 knapsack DP.
Iterate capacities from W down to w so each item is used at most once.

title: Minimum Edits
statement: Print the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or replacements needed to turn string a into string b. Either string may be empty.
input_format: Line 1: a (may be empty). Line 2: b (may be empty).
reference_solution:
import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().split("\n")
a = lines[0].strip(); b = lines[1].strip() if len(lines) > 1 else ""
prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
    cur = [i] + [0] * len(b)
    for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
        cur[j] = prev[j - 1] if ca == cb else 1 + min(prev[j - 1], prev[j], cur[j - 1])
    prev = cur
print(prev[-1])
hints: Think about the last character of each string.
2-D DP: dp[i][j] = edits for a[:i] -> b[:j].
Match costs dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise 1 + min(replace, delete, insert).
